info.name: QUORUM API
info.description:
REST API for QUORUM, the meeting room reservation system.

**Getting started**
1. `docker compose up --build` (API on http://localhost:3000, demo data is seeded).
2. Import this collection and the `QUORUM Local` environment.
3. Run **Auth → Login (admin)** and **Auth → Login (employee)**. Tokens are stored automatically in `adminToken` / `employeeToken`.
4. Or run the whole collection (Runner / newman): it is ordered so every request has what it needs.

**Demo accounts** (password `Password123!`): `admin@company.com` (administrator), `alya.ramadhani@company.com` (employee).

**Conventions**
- JSON in, JSON out. Successes: `{ "data": ..., "meta": { page, limit, total, totalPages } }` (`meta` on lists only).
- Errors always: `{ "error": { "status", "code", "message", "details"? } }`. Branch on `code`, show `message`.
- Private endpoints need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Times are `HH:MM` (24h), dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, ids are UUIDs.
- Status codes: 200/201/204 success, 400 validation, 401 not authenticated, 403 not allowed, 404 not found, 409 conflict, 429 rate limited, 500 server error.

request.description:
Public sign-up. Always creates an **employee** (a `role` in the body is ignored). Password: 8-72 chars with a letter and a number. Email is stored lower-case.

Errors: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `409 EMAIL_TAKEN`, `429 RATE_LIMITED`.

exec: pm.test("every bad field is reported", () => pm.expect([...new Set(pm.response.json().error.details.map(d => d.field))]).to.have.members(["name", "email", "password"]));

request.description: `error.details` lists every failing rule: `[{ location, field, message }]`. A field can appear more than once when it breaks several rules (e.g. a password that is too short and has no number).

Returns `{ token, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn, user }`. Saved to `adminToken`.

Errors: `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (same answer for a wrong password and an unknown email), `403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE`.
Saved to `employeeToken`.
Profile of the token's owner. `401 UNAUTHORIZED | INVALID_TOKEN | TOKEN_EXPIRED` without a valid token.

`204` on success. `409 ROOM_HAS_RESERVATIONS` while reservations reference the room: set it to `maintenance` instead.
Unlike public registration, an admin can set `role` and `status`. `409 EMAIL_TAKEN` on a duplicate.
Omitted fields keep their value; `password` is optional. An admin cannot change their **own** role or status (`403`).

exec: pm.test("joined room and user", () => { pm.expect(r.room.name).to.eql("Harbor"); pm.expect(r.startTime).to.eql("10:00"); pm.expect(r.status).to.eql("upcoming"); });

request.description:
Books for the signed-in user. Rules: room must be `available`; participants ≤ capacity; within working hours (08:00-18:00); not in the past; no overlap with another non-cancelled booking of that room (back-to-back is fine).

Admins may add `userId` to book on someone's behalf (employees get `403`).

Errors: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `404 NOT_FOUND`, `409 RESERVATION_CONFLICT` (with `details.conflictingReservation`), `409 ROOM_UNAVAILABLE`, `409 USER_INACTIVE`.

query.description: date | startTime | createdAt | title | status; prefix - for descending

request.description: Employees are always scoped to their own reservations.
`404` also when it belongs to someone else (existence is not leaked).
Edit an **upcoming** reservation; omitted fields keep their value. Moving it re-runs the booking rules. `409 RESERVATION_LOCKED` once completed or cancelled.
Status changes travel alone. Owners can only cancel; only admins can mark a booking completed.
